title: Oven Over Temperature
fullDescription: Lincoln Impinger conveyor ovens lock out at E1 when the cavity exceeds safety limits. Causes include stuck contactor, runaway gas valve, or thermocouple short.

fixSteps.title: Power down
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and gas before service.

fixSteps.title: Inspect contactor / valve
fixSteps.instruction: Test contactor for welded contacts; gas units check valve closure.

whenToCallPro: Gas valve and high-voltage work requires certified service.

faq.a: Yes, until E1 is fixed; runaway heat is a fire risk.

title: Open Thermocouple
fullDescription: E2 indicates the cavity thermocouple is open or out of range. The controller will not allow heating without valid feedback.

fixSteps.title: Inspect TC connection
fixSteps.instruction: Check polarity and tightness at controller.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermocouple
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM K-type per service manual.

whenToCallPro: If new TC still fails, controller diagnosis required.

faq.a: Yes; reversed polarity gives wrong readings on K-type TCs.

title: Conveyor Speed Fault
shortDescription: Conveyor not running at commanded speed.
fullDescription: Impinger ovens monitor conveyor RPM via a sensor. E3 fires when commanded speed is not achieved, often from belt drag, drive motor failure, or loose tension.

fixSteps.title: Clean and free belt
fixSteps.instruction: Remove debris and crumbs; verify belt moves freely.

fixSteps.title: Inspect drive chain/sprocket
fixSteps.instruction: Check chain tension and sprocket wear.

fixSteps.title: Test motor
fixSteps.instruction: Verify drive motor and speed sensor signals.

faq.a: Yes; debris in the belt path is a leading cause of E3.

title: Air Blower Fault
fullDescription: Impinger ovens move heated air through fingers onto product. E4 fires if the blower stalls or feedback is missing. Without airflow, the oven cannot bake correctly and may overheat.

fixSteps.title: Test motor and capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Verify motor windings and replace capacitor if out of spec.

fixSteps.title: Check air pressure switch
fixSteps.instruction: Verify switch closes when blower runs.

faq.a: Confirms airflow before heat is enabled.

title: Ignition Failure (Gas)
fullDescription: Gas Impinger ovens use a hot-surface or spark ignition. E5 fires when ignition is not confirmed within trial-for-ignition. Causes include closed gas, failed ignitor, dirty flame sensor.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm shutoffs open, supply pressure correct (test at manometer).

fixSteps.title: Inspect ignitor/sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace cracked ignitor; clean flame rod with fine emery.

whenToCallPro: Gas system work should be done by qualified service.

faq.a: Shut off supply, ventilate, do not operate switches, call gas tech.

title: Element Open (Electric)
fullDescription: On electric Impingers, E6 detects an open heating element. Without the full element bank, oven cannot reach setpoint.

fixSteps.title: Test element
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; measure resistance; replace if open.

whenToCallPro: Element replacement involves disassembly and high voltage; consider tech.

faq.a: Often slow preheat or uneven baking.

title: Cooling Fan Fault
fullDescription: Lincoln ovens use a small electronics cooling fan. E7 fires when it stalls. Risk of board overheating.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; install new cooling fan.

faq.a: On the rear/side of control housing; consult manual.

title: Belt Tension / Conveyor Stalled
fullDescription: E8 indicates the conveyor belt is binding or the take-up has lost tension. Cleaning, alignment, and chain inspection are required.

fixSteps.title: Realign belt
fixSteps.instruction: Cool oven, remove belt, reinstall per manual procedure ensuring proper tension.

whenToCallPro: Belt replacement and alignment is operator level once trained.

faq.a: Several years if cleaned; daily cleaning prevents premature wear.

title: Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Supply voltage too high or too low.
fullDescription: E9 indicates voltage outside nameplate range. Continued operation can damage motors and inverters.

fixSteps.title: Measure supply
fixSteps.instruction: Verify voltage at terminal block under load.

faq.a: Yes, surges and brownouts both shorten control life.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Display lost communication with main board.
fullDescription: E10 indicates a broken communication link. Loose harness, moisture, or board failure are typical.
